title: Heartbeat request
description: POST /api/v1/heartbeat (FR-1.2). The host is identified by the credential, never by a field in the body.

schema_version.description: Payload schema version. This directory is version 1.

hostname.description: Hostname as the agent sees it, or null if unreadable. Informational; the credential identifies the host.

uptime_seconds.description: Seconds since the agent process started.

agent_time.description: Agent clock, RFC 3339 UTC. Stored for display only; never used for liveness.

tasks.description: Remote task capabilities (FR-3.1, P3-A01): what this agent can run and what its VM's own configuration enables. The server offers a host a task type only when it is in both supported and enabled, and the host reports local_config valid. Absent means the host offers nothing, as for an agent older than Phase 3. Sent on every heartbeat; it changes only when the agent restarts with another config or version.

catalog_version.description: The catalog_version of the task catalog compiled into the agent (docs/api/tasks/task-catalog.json).

supported.description: Catalog task types this agent version can run, each once. Type ids, not an enum: a newer agent may know types this server does not, and the server ignores those.

enabled.description: Catalog task types the VM's local configuration enables ([tasks] enabled; DEC-14), each once. Empty when local_config is invalid. May list a type the agent does not support yet.

allowed_services.description: The services the VM's local configuration allows restart_service to restart ([tasks] allowed_services; DEC-15), each once, sorted. Empty when local_config is invalid or none is listed. The server leaves out a host whose list lacks the service before sending anything (owner, P3-D01 Q7); the agent still checks its own list when a task arrives.

local_config.description: valid, or invalid when the agent refused the [tasks] section of its config: then nothing is enabled until the owner fixes it on the VM.

recovery.description: Present only while the agent runs in recovery mode (#180, ADR 0030): it kept failing on a version it had already confirmed, so there was nothing to roll back, and systemd started fleet-agent-recovery.service. In recovery mode the agent only sends heartbeats and update results and installs a signed agent update; it sends no report and polls for no task. Absent means normal mode. Only systemd on the VM starts recovery mode; no response field can.

entered_at.description: When this recovery episode began, by the agent's clock (RFC 3339 UTC). Kept while the agent tries normal mode again and falls back. Display only.

reason.description: Why the agent kept failing, as plain text from the agent: its own record of why it stopped (for example a loop that panicked) and what systemd said. One line: no C0 or C1 control characters, no line or paragraph separator (U+2028, U+2029), and no bidirectional formatting characters (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069). Shown to operators as agent text.

not.description: The characters the description rules out. Written as a search, not an anchored pattern, because validators disagree on what ^ and $ match around a newline.

retry_at.description: When the agent will next try normal mode again by itself (about an hour after recovery mode started), by the agent's clock. Display only.

units.description: Which of the installer's systemd units are set up on the VM (#232), as systemd has loaded them, checked by the agent at each heartbeat. Absent means the agent does not say (an older agent); the server stores it as not reported. Unknown fields inside are ignored, so later agents can add more.

recovery.description: true when recovery mode is set up (ADR 0030): fleet-agent-recovery.service carries the installer's marker and is loaded from /etc/systemd/system, fleet-agent.service names it in OnFailure= (drop-ins included), and neither waits for a daemon-reload. false when it is not. null when the agent could not check (it cannot read the unit file, or systemctl does not answer); the dashboard shows that apart from false. A host without recovery mode keeps stopping for good after a crash loop on a confirmed version, until a confirmed update or `fleet-agent install --refresh-units` installs and loads the units.

process.description: The agent process and its systemd service (#251), so the server can see an agent that systemd keeps restarting, for example after a kill at its memory limit, although each process heartbeats normally. The agent reads it once per process, not per heartbeat: the start time is its own, restarts is read with one systemctl show when the process starts, and last_stop is the record the service's ExecStopPost= wrote when the process before this one stopped. Absent means the agent does not say (an older agent). Unknown fields inside are ignored, so later agents can add more.

started_at.description: When this agent process started, by the agent's clock (RFC 3339 UTC, milliseconds). Fixed for the life of the process, so a new value means a new process. Display only, and never used for liveness. In recovery mode it is the recovery process's start.

restarts.description: systemd's NRestarts for fleet-agent.service: how many times systemd restarted it by itself (Restart=) since it was last started any other way. A start by a person, an agent update, recovery mode's hourly try, or a boot sets it to 0. null when the agent could not read it (systemctl failed or did not answer); it tries again at the next heartbeat.

last_stop.description: How the agent process before this one stopped, as systemd told the service's ExecStopPost= ($SERVICE_RESULT, $EXIT_CODE, $EXIT_STATUS: the Result, ExecMainCode, and ExecMainStatus of that run, which systemd resets when the service starts again). null when there is no record: units from before #251, which have no ExecStopPost=, or a record that could not be read.

result.description: systemd's result for the run: success, exit-code, signal, core-dump, watchdog, timeout, oom-kill (killed at the unit's MemoryMax=), resources, protocol, start-limit-hit, or a word a later systemd adds. Checked by pattern, not an enum, so a new word does not fail the heartbeat.

exit_code.description: How the main process ended: exited (exit_status is its exit status), killed or dumped (exit_status is the signal's number, 9 for SIGKILL). null when systemd did not say, as when the process never started.

exit_status.description: The exit status (0 to 255), or the signal's number for killed or dumped (1 to 64). null with exit_code null, or for a signal the agent does not know.

stopped_at.description: When the record was written, just after the process stopped, by the agent's clock (RFC 3339 UTC). Display only.
